newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives won't join EMU-former party chief.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives won't join EMU-former party chief.

text.p: A Conservative government would never take Britain into a single European currency, former Conservative Party Chairman Norman Tebbit said on Thursday.
"There's no enthusiasts, as I see it, for the single currency either in the Conservative Party nor indeed in Germany," he told BBC radio 4.

The Conservatives face a general election on May 1, which they are expected to lose to the opposition Labour party. But Tebbit argues a public statement against European Monetary Union could boost support.

"Perhaps the government is now coming into a position where, whatever the niceties to cover some divisions, it's going to be pretty clear to the electors that a Conservative governemnt would not enter a single currency," he said.

"I think we've had another useful indication of where the government's going from Malcolm Rifkind, the Foreign Secretary, who yesterday denounced the single currency in principle as likely to divide Europe for 25 years. That's very good progress,"

Tebbit said that Prime Minister John Major was privately opposed to EMU and did not support the policy propounded by Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke that Britain should "wait and see" whether to participate when EMU actually starts.
He added that Clarke, one of the most prominent pro-Europeans, was not fully convinced of the benefits of EMU.

"What Ken is saying is you could still go in without losing sovereignty -- I disagree with him about that -- but he says I haven't made up my mind whether it's a good thing or not. That's not wild enthusiasm."
Tebbit is one of the most outspoken Eurosceptics and has been openly critical of Major's administration.

In Thursday's edition of the tabloid newspaper The Sun, he said he understood why the paper abandoned its traditional support for the Conservatives and switched to the opposition Labour party earlier this week.
"Time and time again The Sun has asked the Prime Minister to get off the fence over the European single currency - but he will not."
He also said the current Conservative administration was not the best Britain had ever had but "it is better by far than any Labour government we have ever had."
